A hidden gem in Ho Chi Minh
May 2016 • Friends
The gem of a find is tucked away on a small road in District 3 of HCM. The owner turned his family home into a Food Intersection & Lounge. The space has lots of character. You get an artistic feel and the food is Vietnamese food with a twist given a modern day's interpretation. The deco is beautiful with a nice courtyard. I have to say the owner has excellent taste. Every corner and floor gives a feel of something pulled out from an ID magazine. It's a small and quaint space that you will like. Better make reservations. Oh yes, the close on Mondays and Tuesdays.

Comfortable, elegant, neat
Aug 2015 • Friends
There are many types of restaurants - some fast food, others fine dining, others casual dining and so on. Each kind offers a different type of service or cuisine, and may attract different clientele based on those.

Comfortable, elegant, neat are my first feeling when coming through the red door. The servers are pleasant, friendly although not very professional. The menu is not so long, not make you difficult in choosing what you want. Everything is properly cooked, I like most of the dishes in collecting menu. The flavor are well balanced...

Stay inside the dining room, enjoy the food & drinks, looking through glass doors, different trees & good decor of RedDoor make me really relaxed after hard working nearly all day

Someone says the price like 5 stars. If you combine the atmosphere & the cleanliness of the restaurant, the warming & friendly of the boss & employees and excellent collection menu, I think it's worth for that price

Amazing, elegant and delicious modern Vietnamese food
May 2015 • Couples
I love this place and recommend it to all visitors and residents -- for me it's one of the most interesting restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City. They break classic Vietnamese dishes down and build them up again, or accentuate something at the very heart of the dish, to create something very elegant, very thoughtful, and most importantly delicious. The plating is very nicely done, too. 

I look at it as a big tasting menu. Two people can share 5, 6 dishes easy. The desserts are well worth sampling. I wouldn't mind a little more variety on the wine but all in all, this place is definitely worth visiting for any foodie living in HCMC or passing through. It's not in District 1 but really not that far, and regardless, well worth the trip.

Oddly (and amazingly) interesting experience!
Jul 2015 • Friends
I was recommended by a friend to dine at Red Door and Red Door indeed did not disappoint. A fusion of traditional and modern Vietnamese dishes served beautifully and appetizingly on a plate. The portion is moderate but the quality is undeniably tasty; this is probably to make sure you try all three courses because they are all extremely delicious (amazing choices for appetizers and desserts- especially signature flan in home-brewed white rice alcohol, not to mention a well-selected collection of wine). This restaurant is a treat to the stomach and to the eyes: a place with an interesting, minimalist concept; this is truly a quiet & classy, very enjoyable corner of busy Saigon. Definitely coming back with excitement to try other dishes on the menu (we had the lotus salad, ribs and seafood noodles, and signature flan - my friend before tried the beef stew which, according to him, was "to die for"). Staff are friendly and helpful. Atmosphere is an A+!
